Subject: Re: Intro & demo - follow-up/next steps

Thanks for the demo today, Ben — appreciate the deep dive. Quick recap from our side and a couple of asks so we can scope implementation: 

- We want to use Redwood for semantic search + reranker for our support KB (embedding + rerank stage).
- Want to route high-priority customer queries to a low-latency, higher-cost model; everything else to a cheaper quantized model.
- Authentication and SDK setup: our infra team needs best-practices for long-lived tokens vs short-lived, and server-side vs client-side calls.
- Concerned about rate limits: we expect bursty traffic (up to ~120 req/s peak) with many retries; want guidance on 429 handling, idempotency, and recommended backoff strategies.

Can you send a short mutual action plan + recommended SDK config and example retry logic? Also, please include any artifacts for our security team.

— Sam

Sam — thanks for the clear asks. Below is a concise mutual action plan and draft recommendations we discussed. I attached a short PDF (redwood-rate-limit-guidelines.pdf) with sample backoff, idempotency patterns, and SDK snippets.

Mutual Action Plan (next 2 weeks):
1) Architecture design session (internal + ACME platform) — target: 2026-12-03. Owner: Marissa.
2) Security/compliance packet for ACME security review — Ben to send SSO/KMS doc + SOC2 checklist by 2026-12-02.
3) Integration pilot (embeddings + reranker) — ACME to run a 1-week pilot with 50k queries/day. Owner: Sam/Priya.
4) Rate-limit & retry test: ACME to run synthetic load test; Redwood will provide guidance and sample harness. Owner: Rishi/Aditya.

High-level integration recommendations:
- SDK/auth: Use server-side API keys stored in a secret store (short rotation is fine). For client-side uses, route calls through your backend to avoid exposing keys. We support token-based keys + optional mTLS for Private deployments.
- Routing: Use per-route config in Redwood to map intents to model variants (e.g., /chat/high-priority -> high-throughput, low-latency pool). You can define routing policy by latency SLO or cost tier; we'll share sample route YAML in the drive.
- Structured output / tool calling: Recommend using Redwood's function-calling + schema validation to produce structured JSON for downstream services (we'll attach an example that maps to your reranker pipeline).
- Embeddings & reranker: Batch embeddings at up to 8-16 items per request for throughput; persist vectors in your vector DB and use the Redwood reranker step for final scoring.

Rate-limits, retries & idempotency (summary):
- 429 handling: Apply exponential backoff with jitter; do not retry non-idempotent mutate requests by default.
- Backoff policy (recommended): initial_delay=200ms, multiplier=2, max_delay=10s, with full jitter. Cap retries at 5 for idempotent calls.
- Idempotency: Attach a client-generated request_id header for operations that may be retried; Redwood will de-dupe idempotent requests when request_id is provided and the operation is eligible.
- Quotas: Per-account and per-route soft quota + hard quota enforcement. We'll provide a preview of expected throttling at your projected peak.

Action items from Redwood:
- Marissa: schedule design session with ACME platform (target 12/3).
- Rishi/Aditya: produce a short load-test plan and sample retry logic (JS + Python) by 12/2.
- Ben: send security docs + share Drive link to sample route configs.

I've attached the rate-limit guidelines and a dataset snapshot you can use for the pilot. Let us know if you want us to run a controlled load test against a staging endpoint.

Best,
Ben

Sam — looping in Rishi/Aditya for the ops checklist. Quick notes ahead of the design session: 

1) SDK snippets: We recommend server-side usage of our official SDK (node/python) with built-in retry helpers. Example config (conceptual):
   - maxRetries: 5
   - retryableStatusCodes: [429, 503]
   - idempotencyHeader: X-Redwood-Request-Id

2) Auth patterns: Issue short-lived API keys rotated every 30 days; for stricter environments use our Private deployment with customer KMS.

3) Routing & fallbacks: Define two model routes: "prod-lowcost" (quantized) and "prod-lowlatency" (FP16). Use a request header X-ACME-Priority to route; set a fallback: if low-latency pool is saturated, automatically route to low-cost after a 200ms tail-latency threshold.

4) Rate-limit observability: Redwood Console exposes per-route token-level metrics; we can create a shared dashboard for ACME.

I added proposed meeting time slots to the Drive folder.

— Marissa

Sam/Priya — attaching a short load-test plan inline and a JS retry example.

Load-test plan (summary):
- Goal: validate behavior at peak (120 req/s) and burst (300 req/s) for embedding and reranker endpoints.
- Setup: ACME will run synthetic clients from two regions; Redwood will provide a staging model route and expected rate-limit headers.
- Observables: 429 rate, per-route tail-latency, success rate after retries, de-dupe effectiveness for request_id.

JS retry example (pseudo):

const MAX_RETRIES = 5;
async function callWithRetry(fn) {
  let attempt = 0;
  let delay = 200; // ms
  while (attempt <= MAX_RETRIES) {
    const requestId = generateRequestId(); // attach X-Redwood-Request-Id
    try {
      return await fn({ headers: { 'X-Redwood-Request-Id': requestId } });
    } catch (err) {
      if (!isRetryable(err) || attempt === MAX_RETRIES) throw err;
      // full jitter: sleep(random(0, delay))
      await sleep(Math.floor(Math.random() * delay));
      delay = Math.min(delay * 2, 10000);
      attempt += 1;
    }
  }
}

Notes: mark embedding-only calls as idempotent (safe to retry). For single-shot generation requests that mutate user-visible state, require client-side dedupe via request_id before retrying.

I'll join the 12/3 session and bring the staging endpoints.

1) For our reranker flow we expect many small embedding calls + one reranker call per query. Do you recommend treating the reranker call as idempotent? We plan to store request_id at the aggregator layer either way.
2) For client-side UX we sometimes want optimistic retries in the browser (e.g., intermittent network glitches). Any guidance on exposing safe retry surface to frontend?

If you can add short examples for (1) and (2) to the Drive, that would be great. Otherwise we'll prep our infra folks for the synthetic load test on Monday.

Cheers,
